theme: Advanced channel / Donchian breakout (Highest/Lowest core) — continuation AND false-break fade.

specs.name: DonchianCloseBreakUpper
specs.rule: Long when Close crosses above prior-N-bar Highest-of-High (confirmed, shift 1)
specs.hypothesis: Close exiting the prior-N-bar high range yields positive forward N-bar returns; a genuine range-to-trend ignition.
specs.economic_rationale: Stop clusters and resting breakout orders just beyond multi-week extremes trigger a one-sided liquidity cascade (Turtle/Donchian).
specs.orthogonality: Close-confirmed channel break; distinct from intrabar-pierce sibling and from MA-cross trend blocks.
specs.source: Faith, Way of the Turtle (2007); Clenow, Following the Trend (2013).
specs.notes: Highest #ComputedFrom#=High(2), #Shift#=1 = Donchian upper. Short mirror: Close crosses below Lowest(Low).

specs.name: DonchianHighPierceUpper
specs.rule: Long when current High pierces above prior-N-bar Highest-of-High (intrabar, channel at shift 1)
specs.hypothesis: Intrabar pierce triggers earlier than a close break; extra entry edge offsets extra MAE in fast ignitions.
specs.economic_rationale: Resting buy-stops fill the instant the level is touched — the cascade is an intrabar event.
specs.orthogonality: Touch-vs-close counterpart to DonchianCloseBreakUpper; lets the search pick the confirmation per instrument.
specs.notes: is_greater(High[0], Highest(High,N)[1]) — channel shift1 confirmed, no leak. Short: Low < Lowest(Low).

specs.name: FailedHighBreakFade
specs.rule: Short when Close crosses back below prior-N-bar Highest-of-High (false-break reversion)
specs.hypothesis: Re-entering the range by crossing back below the just-exceeded high yields negative forward returns; failed breaks snap back.
specs.economic_rationale: Late longs who chased the level are trapped; forced liquidation fuels the reversion (bull-trap).
specs.orthogonality: Same level as the breakout blocks, opposite trade — captures that most channel breaks fail in ranges.
specs.source: Cooper, Hit and Run Trading (1996); Connors & Alvarez (2008).
specs.notes: crosses_below(Close, Highest(High,N)[1]) encodes 'was above, now below' in one cross. Long mirror = reclaim of the lower channel.

specs.name: ChannelMidlineBias
specs.rule: Long when Close > DonchianChannels Middle line
specs.hypothesis: Price above the centre of its recent realised range shows positive forward autocorrelation; midline = parameter-light trend proxy.
specs.economic_rationale: Range midpoint is an outlier-resistant fair-value anchor; persistent location above it = sustained net buying.
specs.orthogonality: Uses DonchianChannels Middle (multi-output) — range-midpoint bias distinct from edge-break and MA filters.
specs.notes: DonchianChannels is multi-output (Upper=0,Middle=1,Lower=2). VERIFY line indexing on import. Best as a bias slot.

specs.name: VolGatedChannelBreak
specs.rule: Long when Close breaks above prior-N-bar Highest AND ATRPercentRank is in a low-vol regime
specs.hypothesis: Channel breaks emerging from low volatility have higher forward expectancy than breaks in already-elevated vol (fresh transition vs late extension).
specs.economic_rationale: Volatility compresses as a balanced auction coils; the release of that coil is the highest-information channel event.
specs.orthogonality: The one intentional conjunction — 'low-vol regime AND level break' is one named setup; ATRPercentRank self-normalises (mid 50), portable.
specs.notes: ATRPercentRank is ✦ custom, percentile 0-100, mid 50 — a 40 ceiling is meaningful. #Lenght# preserves Java typo.

specs.name: RangeExpansionThrust
specs.rule: Long when current BarRange exceeds BiggestRange of the prior N bars (expansion ignition)
specs.hypothesis: A bar with the largest range in N signals expansion ignition; forward returns continue in the expansion direction briefly.
specs.economic_rationale: Outsized range = sudden imbalance overwhelming resting liquidity (Crabel expansion/ORB); imbalances persist briefly.
specs.orthogonality: Pure range-geometry expansion, no level reference — width-based trigger complementing level breaks.
specs.notes: is_greater(BarRange[0], BiggestRange(N)[1]); both pricerange. Direction-blind — opposite block selects down case. Likely a filter.

specs.name: ChannelSqueezeNarrow
specs.rule: Filter: BBWidthRatio below threshold (channel unusually tight)
specs.hypothesis: Contracting envelope raises the probability of imminent expansion; as a gate it raises breakout hit-rate.
specs.economic_rationale: Width contraction is the vol-clustering signature of a coiling auction; low dispersion precedes a regime shift.
specs.orthogonality: Symmetric regime gate (CBlock_null); BBWidthRatio = native channel-width-vs-baseline ratio, cleanest squeeze proxy without arithmetic.
specs.notes: Substitution for Highest-Lowest width (needs Minus op). Self-normalising; threshold portable. VERIFY BBWidthRatio scale on import.

specs.name: DonchianLowerReclaimLong
specs.rule: Long when Close crosses back above prior-N-bar Lowest-of-Low (lower-channel false-break reclaim)
specs.hypothesis: Reclaiming the prior-N-bar low it broke below yields positive forward returns — bear-trap reversion.
specs.economic_rationale: A failed downside break traps late shorts; short-covering supplies upside fuel (long twin of FailedHighBreakFade).
specs.orthogonality: Lowest(Low) reclaim; support-side counterpart to FailedHighBreakFade. Level-defined, not OB/OS.
specs.notes: crosses_above(Close, Lowest(Low,N)[1]). Short mirror = crosses_below the upper channel.
